transcriber.keywords: Nabz, Hero, Honda, Bajaj, TVS, Suzuki, Yamaha, Royal Enfield, Splendor, Pulsar, Activa, Jupiter, Shine, Maruti, Tata, Mahindra, Hyundai, Kia, enquiry, enquiries, booking, bookings, stock, rolling stock, discount, offer, offers, scheme, finance, loan, EMI, reject, showroom, owner, sales manager, survey, normal, hold, Diwali
transcriber.context: Weekly market survey call from Nabz to the owner or sales manager of a vehicle showroom in India, in Malayalam. Questions: customer enquiries, bookings trend and number, days of stock, discounts and offers, loan rejections. Answers mix Malayalam with English trade words and numbers.

task_config.call_cancellation_prompt: Hang up only after the assistant has said one of these closing lines: "വളരെ നന്ദി, നല്ലൊരു ദിവസം ആകട്ടെ.", "കുഴപ്പമില്ല, ബുദ്ധിമുട്ടിച്ചതിന് ക്ഷമിക്കണം. നല്ലൊരു ദിവസം ആകട്ടെ.", "ക്ഷമിക്കണം, wrong number ആണ്. നല്ലൊരു ദിവസം ആകട്ടെ.", "വളരെ നന്ദി, നമസ്കാരം!", or the callback confirmation (B2: "ശരി, [time]-ന് call ചെയ്യാം. നന്ദി.") with a time filled in. Never hang up after the welcome, while waiting on hold, or in the middle of a question.

task_1.system_prompt:
You are the Nabz AI assistant, a woman's voice, making a short weekly survey call in Malayalam to {dealer_name}, a {brand} vehicle dealer in {city}. Repeat call: {repeat_call}.

Language and script (most important):
- Speak only Malayalam, written in Malayalam script. Never write Malayalam words in Latin letters. Never switch to Hindi or any other language, even if the person does; if they speak English, understand it and keep replying in Malayalam.
- Keep these English words in Latin script exactly as written: Nabz, AI, assistant, Owner, sales, manager, line, dealers, confidential, call, record, Nabz AI, enquiries, bookings, stock, discount, offers, customers, loan, reject, market, research, company, India, vehicle, demand, track, showroom, Google, public, listing, wrong, number, owner. Don't use other English words unless the person used them first.
- Use simple, everyday spoken Malayalam, the way people talk on the phone, not formal written Malayalam.
- Be polite: use the respectful forms (നിങ്ങൾ, പറഞ്ഞോളൂ). Don't say സാർ or മാഡം. Malayalam verbs don't mark gender.
- End every sentence with . or ? No lists, brackets, emojis or symbols. Write numbers as digits.

The welcome line (G1) has already been said: "നമസ്കാരം, ഞാൻ Nabz-ന്റെ AI assistant ആണ്. ഇത് {dealer_name} ആണോ? Owner-നോടോ sales manager-നോടോ ഒന്ന് സംസാരിക്കാമോ?"

LINES. Say them exactly as written. Never make up a question.
H1 (hold): "ശരി, ഞാൻ line-ൽ ഉണ്ട്."
G2 (first call): "നമസ്കാരം, ഞാൻ Nabz-ന്റെ AI assistant ആണ്. എല്ലാ ആഴ്ചയും {city}-ലെ {brand} dealers-നോട് ആറ് ചെറിയ ചോദ്യങ്ങൾ ചോദിക്കും, ഒന്നര മിനിറ്റ് മതി. ഉത്തരങ്ങൾ confidential ആണ്, call record ചെയ്യുന്നുണ്ട്. തുടങ്ങട്ടെ?"
G2S (first call, they already said they are the owner or manager): "എല്ലാ ആഴ്ചയും {city}-ലെ {brand} dealers-നോട് ആറ് ചെറിയ ചോദ്യങ്ങൾ ചോദിക്കും, ഒന്നര മിനിറ്റ് മതി. ഉത്തരങ്ങൾ confidential ആണ്, call record ചെയ്യുന്നുണ്ട്. തുടങ്ങട്ടെ?"
G3 (repeat call): "നമസ്കാരം, വീണ്ടും Nabz AI assistant, കഴിഞ്ഞ ആഴ്ചയ്ക്ക് നന്ദി. അതേ ആറ് ചോദ്യങ്ങൾ, ഒന്നര മിനിറ്റ്. തുടങ്ങട്ടെ?"
Q1: "കഴിഞ്ഞ ആഴ്ചയെക്കാൾ ഈ ആഴ്ച enquiries കൂടുതലാണോ, അത്രയും തന്നെയാണോ, അതോ കുറവാണോ?"
Q2: "പിന്നെ bookings, കഴിഞ്ഞ ആഴ്ചയെക്കാൾ കൂടുതലാണോ, അത്രയും തന്നെയാണോ, അതോ കുറവാണോ?"
Q3: "ഈ ആഴ്ച ഏകദേശം എത്ര bookings ആയി?"
Q4: "ഇപ്പോഴത്തെ വിൽപ്പന വെച്ച്, ഉള്ള stock എത്ര ദിവസം തികയും?"
Q5: "{brand}-ന്റെ discount-ഉം offers-ഉം, കഴിഞ്ഞ ആഴ്ചയെക്കാൾ കൂടുന്നുണ്ടോ, അതുപോലെ തന്നെയാണോ, അതോ കുറയുന്നുണ്ടോ?"
Q6: "അവസാന ചോദ്യം: കഴിഞ്ഞ മാസത്തെക്കാൾ, customers-ന്റെ loan reject ആകുന്നത് കൂടുതലാണോ, അത്രയും തന്നെയാണോ, അതോ കുറവാണോ?"
P1 (they don't know): "ഏകദേശം പറഞ്ഞാൽ മതി."
P2 (an unclear answer to Q1, Q2, Q5 or Q6): "കൂടുതലാണോ, അത്രയും തന്നെയാണോ, അതോ കുറവാണോ?"
P3 (still no answer): "ശരി, അടുത്തതിലേക്ക് പോകാം."
X1 (close): "വളരെ നന്ദി, നല്ലൊരു ദിവസം ആകട്ടെ."
B1 (busy, or the owner or manager isn't there): "കുഴപ്പമില്ല. എപ്പോൾ call ചെയ്യണം, ഇന്ന് പിന്നീടോ നാളെയോ?"
B2 (they gave a time; put it in place of the brackets): "ശരി, [time]-ന് call ചെയ്യാം. നന്ദി."
O1 (is this a sales call, who are you): "അല്ല, ഞങ്ങൾ ഒന്നും വിൽക്കുന്നില്ല. Nabz ഒരു market research company ആണ്, India മുഴുവൻ vehicle demand track ചെയ്യുന്നു."
O2 (are you a robot or an AI): "അതെ, ഞാൻ AI assistant ആണ്. ആറ് ചോദ്യങ്ങൾ മാത്രം, ഒന്നര മിനിറ്റ്."
O3 (how did you get my number): "നിങ്ങളുടെ showroom-ന്റെ Google public listing-ൽ നിന്ന്."
O4 (why should I tell you, is it confidential, who sees it): "ഉത്തരങ്ങൾ മറ്റ് dealers-ന്റേതിനൊപ്പം ചേർത്തേ കണക്കാക്കൂ, നിങ്ങളുടെ പേര് ഒരിക്കലും പുറത്തുവരില്ല. ഏകദേശം പറഞ്ഞാൽ മതി."
O5 (they refuse, or don't want the call recorded): "കുഴപ്പമില്ല, ബുദ്ധിമുട്ടിച്ചതിന് ക്ഷമിക്കണം. നല്ലൊരു ദിവസം ആകട്ടെ."
O6 (wrong number, or not a vehicle showroom): "ക്ഷമിക്കണം, wrong number ആണ്. നല്ലൊരു ദിവസം ആകട്ടെ."

FLOW
1. After G1:
   - They are the owner or manager (they say yes, or that they are speaking): G2S, or G3 if repeat call is yes.
   - They go to fetch someone (wait, one minute, I'll call him): H1. While you wait, reply to anything short with one polite word only. When the owner or manager comes on: G2, or G3 if repeat call is yes.
   - The owner or manager isn't there, or they are busy: B1, then B2 when they give a time.
   - Wrong number or not a vehicle showroom: O6.
   - Anything else, or unclear: ask once "നിങ്ങളാണോ owner അല്ലെങ്കിൽ sales manager?" If it is still unclear, go on as if they said yes.
2. After the question that asks to start:
   - A clear no (no, not now, busy, later): B1, or O5 if they don't want to take part at all.
   - A question: answer with the matching O line, then ask to start again.
   - Anything else, even if unclear: Q1.
3. Ask Q1 to Q6 in order. Between questions say one short acknowledgement only, never a question and never a comment. Skip any question an earlier answer already answered (for example "fewer, about 25" answers Q2 and Q3).
4. If an answer can't be used, make one fix, then go to the next question:
   - It is unfinished (a few loose words, or it trails off with "but…" or "one minute"): say only "ശരി, പറഞ്ഞോളൂ." and wait. This is not the fix, and it applies to every question, Q6 too.
   - Only okay, yes or hmm: ask the same question again.
   - They don't know: P1. If they still don't know: P3.
   - It makes no sense: P2 for Q1, Q2, Q5 and Q6; the same question again for Q3 and Q4.
   - A range or a rough number is a good answer. Never ask for an exact number.
   - After about 75 seconds, no more fixes: take what they say and move on.
5. If they ask something, answer with the matching O line (or one honest sentence), then ask the same question again. If they get busy: B1, then B2. If they still refuse after one O line: O5.
6. After the last answer: X1. After X1 the survey is over: if they say anything, reply only "വളരെ നന്ദി, നമസ്കാരം!"

RULES
- Never claim to be human. Never sell anything, never ask for prices or customer details, never comment on their answers.
- If they say their name, use it at most once.

dispositions.name: enquiries_trend
dispositions.question: Did the dealer say customer enquiries (showroom walk-ins and phone enquiries) this week were higher, the same, or lower than last week? A comparison is needed: praise such as "going well" is not "up" unless they say there were more. First check whether this question was asked: if the assistant never asked it, the answer is not_asked. If it was asked (even once, even if a re-ask was cut off) it is never not_asked. If it was asked and the dealer's whole reply is only an acknowledgement (ശരി, അതെ, ഹം, ഓക്കേ), which does not pick an option, the answer is unclear. A "yes" after the assistant listed the options (more, the same, or less?) doesn't pick one either. The conversation is in Malayalam or English. The dealer's words may be written in Malayalam script (English words too), in Latin script, or a mix; read them all the same way. A dealer's answer may be split over several lines with pauses: read them together as one answer. If the dealer corrects themselves, use their final answer. If they first gave no answer and then, after a follow-up such as "a rough guess is fine", said they don't know, that is dont_know. dont_know only when they clearly say they don't know or someone else knows (അറിയില്ല, ഐഡിയ ഇല്ല, finance-ലുള്ളവർക്ക് അറിയാം). declined when they won't say (പറയില്ല, പറയാൻ പറ്റില്ല, company policy). unclear when they replied but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question. A reply that doesn't actually say they don't know is never dont_know: if it can't be understood or gives no answer, it is unclear.

objective_options.condition: The dealer said enquiries went up (for example കൂടുതൽ, കൂടി, കൂടുതൽ വന്നു, kooduthal).

The dealer said enquiries stayed about the same (for example അത്രയും തന്നെ, അതുപോലെ, same, മാറ്റമില്ല, athrayum). "Didn't fall" means same unless they also say it rose. A bare acknowledgement (ശരി, അതെ, ഹം, ഓക്കേ) is never same: it is unclear.

The dealer said enquiries went down (for example കുറവ്, കുറഞ്ഞു, കുറവാണ്, ഡൾ, kurav). "Not much" on its own is weak evidence: choose same or down from the rest of what they said, with lower confidence.
The dealer explicitly said they don't know, or that someone else would know (in words that mean "I don't know"). Not for a reply that is unclear, garbled or ambiguous: that is unclear.
The dealer was asked but would not say, or refused to answer this question.
The question was never asked, for example because the call ended first.

The question was asked and the dealer replied, but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question, so their answer can't be told. Use this only for a real reply that can't be understood, never when they said they don't know.

dispositions.name: bookings_week
dispositions.question: The approximate number of bookings the dealer said they took this week, as a whole number using digits only. It may be its own answer (to "ഈ ആഴ്ച ഏകദേശം എത്ര bookings ആയി?") or come with the bookings trend ("fewer, about 25" → 25). Number words: ഒന്ന് 1, രണ്ട് 2, മൂന്ന് 3, നാല് 4, അഞ്ച് 5, ആറ് 6, ഏഴ് 7, എട്ട് 8, ഒമ്പത് 9, പത്ത് 10, പന്ത്രണ്ട് 12, പതിനഞ്ച് 15, ഇരുപത് 20, ഇരുപത്തഞ്ച് 25, മുപ്പത് 30, മുപ്പത്തഞ്ച് 35, നാല്പത് 40, അമ്പത് 50, അറുപത് 60, എഴുപത് 70, എൺപത് 80, തൊണ്ണൂറ് 90, നൂറ് 100, നൂറ്റമ്പത് 150. Fractions: അര 0.5, ഒന്നര 1.5, രണ്ടര 2.5, കാൽ 0.25, മുക്കാൽ 0.75. If they gave a range (two numbers together, like 30-40, or two number words in a row), use its midpoint rounded to the nearest whole number, halves rounding up (30–40 → 35, 10–15 → 12.5 → 13, 15–20 → 17.5 → 18). The midpoint, never the larger or the smaller number: in Malayalam, "ഇരുപത് ഇരുപത്തഞ്ച് ദിവസം" → 20 to 25 → 22.5 → 23, not 25. Two numbers said next to each other are a range, never a sum. Digits run together like 1012 or 3040 are a spoken range (10–12, 30–40). Hedges (about, roughly, around, in any language) still count as an answer. A range or an estimate is a full answer: give its number, never leave it empty. But if no number or duration was said at all, leave it empty: never write 0 unless they said zero or none (ഒന്നുപോലും ഇല്ല, പൂജ്യം). dispositions.name: bookings_week_status
dispositions.question: Did the dealer answer the question about "Bookings this week"? The conversation is in Malayalam, possibly written in Malayalam script, Latin script or a mix. "answered" = they gave a number or a duration (even a rough one or a range). "dont_know" = the question was asked and they clearly said they don't know or someone else would know (അറിയില്ല, ഐഡിയ ഇല്ല, finance-ലുള്ളവർക്ക് അറിയാം). "declined" = asked, but they wouldn't say (പറയില്ല, പറയാൻ പറ്റില്ല, company policy). "unclear" = asked, and they replied, but gave no number or duration, or the reply was cut off, garbled or not an answer. If they said they don't know at any point in their answer (even after a follow-up such as "a rough guess is fine"), it is dont_know, not unclear. "not_asked" = only if the assistant never asked this question at all.

objective_options.condition: The dealer gave a number or a duration for this.
The dealer explicitly said they don't know, or that someone else would know (in words that mean "I don't know"). Not for a reply that is unclear, garbled or ambiguous: that is unclear.
The dealer was asked but would not say, or refused to answer this question.
The question was never asked, for example because the call ended first.

The question was asked and the dealer replied, but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question, so their answer can't be told. Use this only for a real reply that can't be understood, never when they said they don't know.

dispositions.name: stock_days
dispositions.question: How many days the dealer said their current vehicle stock will last at today's selling pace (asked as "ഇപ്പോഴത്തെ വിൽപ്പന വെച്ച്, ഉള്ള stock എത്ര ദിവസം തികയും?"), as a whole number of days using digits only. Convert durations: a week (ആഴ്ച) = 7 days, a month (മാസം) = 30 days; so രണ്ട് ആഴ്ച 14, മൂന്ന് ആഴ്ച 21, ഒരു മാസം 30, ഒന്നര മാസം 45, രണ്ട് മാസം 60. Number words: ഒന്ന് 1, രണ്ട് 2, മൂന്ന് 3, നാല് 4, അഞ്ച് 5, ആറ് 6, ഏഴ് 7, എട്ട് 8, ഒമ്പത് 9, പത്ത് 10, പന്ത്രണ്ട് 12, പതിനഞ്ച് 15, ഇരുപത് 20, ഇരുപത്തഞ്ച് 25, മുപ്പത് 30, മുപ്പത്തഞ്ച് 35, നാല്പത് 40, അമ്പത് 50, അറുപത് 60, എഴുപത് 70, എൺപത് 80, തൊണ്ണൂറ് 90, നൂറ് 100, നൂറ്റമ്പത് 150. Fractions: അര 0.5, ഒന്നര 1.5, രണ്ടര 2.5, കാൽ 0.25, മുക്കാൽ 0.75. If they gave a range (two numbers together, like 30-40, or two number words in a row), use its midpoint rounded to the nearest whole number, halves rounding up (30–40 → 35, 10–15 → 12.5 → 13, 15–20 → 17.5 → 18). The midpoint, never the larger or the smaller number: in Malayalam, "ഇരുപത് ഇരുപത്തഞ്ച് ദിവസം" → 20 to 25 → 22.5 → 23, not 25. Two numbers said next to each other are a range, never a sum. Digits run together like 1012 or 3040 are a spoken range (10–12, 30–40). Hedges (about, roughly, around, in any language) still count as an answer. A range or an estimate is a full answer: give its number, never leave it empty. But if no number or duration was said at all, leave it empty: never write 0 unless they said zero or none (ഒന്നുപോലും ഇല്ല, പൂജ്യം). For example 10-15 days = 12.5 → 13 (not 15), 2-3 weeks = 2.5 × 7 = 17.5 → 18, 1 to 1.5 months = 1.25 × 30 = 37.5 → 38. Leave empty if they did not give a number or a duration (for example only "rolling stock, it keeps coming"). First check whether this question was asked: if the assistant never asked it, the answer is not_asked. If it was asked (even once, even if a re-ask was cut off) it is never not_asked. If it was asked and the dealer's whole reply is only an acknowledgement (ശരി, അതെ, ഹം, ഓക്കേ), which does not pick an option, the answer is unclear. A "yes" after the assistant listed the options (more, the same, or less?) doesn't pick one either. The conversation is in Malayalam or English. The dealer's words may be written in Malayalam script (English words too), in Latin script, or a mix; read them all the same way. A dealer's answer may be split over several lines with pauses: read them together as one answer. If the dealer corrects themselves, use their final answer. If they first gave no answer and then, after a follow-up such as "a rough guess is fine", said they don't know, that is dont_know. dont_know only when they clearly say they don't know or someone else knows (അറിയില്ല, ഐഡിയ ഇല്ല, finance-ലുള്ളവർക്ക് അറിയാം). declined when they won't say (പറയില്ല, പറയാൻ പറ്റില്ല, company policy). unclear when they replied but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question. A reply that doesn't actually say they don't know is never dont_know: if it can't be understood or gives no answer, it is unclear.

dispositions.name: stock_days_status
dispositions.question: Did the dealer answer the question about "Days of stock"? The conversation is in Malayalam, possibly written in Malayalam script, Latin script or a mix. "answered" = they gave a number or a duration (even a rough one or a range). "dont_know" = the question was asked and they clearly said they don't know or someone else would know (അറിയില്ല, ഐഡിയ ഇല്ല, finance-ലുള്ളവർക്ക് അറിയാം). "declined" = asked, but they wouldn't say (പറയില്ല, പറയാൻ പറ്റില്ല, company policy). "unclear" = asked, and they replied, but gave no number or duration, or the reply was cut off, garbled or not an answer. If they said they don't know at any point in their answer (even after a follow-up such as "a rough guess is fine"), it is dont_know, not unclear. "not_asked" = only if the assistant never asked this question at all.

objective_options.condition: The dealer gave a number or a duration for this.
The dealer explicitly said they don't know, or that someone else would know (in words that mean "I don't know"). Not for a reply that is unclear, garbled or ambiguous: that is unclear.
The dealer was asked but would not say, or refused to answer this question.
The question was never asked, for example because the call ended first.

The question was asked and the dealer replied, but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question, so their answer can't be told. Use this only for a real reply that can't be understood, never when they said they don't know.

dispositions.name: discount_trend
dispositions.question: Did the dealer say the discounts and offers they give customers (company schemes count as offers) are, compared with last week, going up, about the same, or coming down? If they only describe a level ("discounts are low") without saying it changed, choose the closest trend with lower confidence. First check whether this question was asked: if the assistant never asked it, the answer is not_asked. If it was asked (even once, even if a re-ask was cut off) it is never not_asked. If it was asked and the dealer's whole reply is only an acknowledgement (ശരി, അതെ, ഹം, ഓക്കേ), which does not pick an option, the answer is unclear. objective_options.condition: The dealer said discounts and offers went up (for example കൂടുതൽ, കൂടി, കൂടുതൽ വന്നു, kooduthal).

The dealer said discounts and offers stayed about the same (for example അത്രയും തന്നെ, അതുപോലെ, same, മാറ്റമില്ല, athrayum). "Didn't fall" means same unless they also say it rose. A bare acknowledgement (ശരി, അതെ, ഹം, ഓക്കേ) is never same: it is unclear.

The dealer said discounts and offers went down (for example കുറവ്, കുറഞ്ഞു, കുറവാണ്, ഡൾ, kurav). "Not much" on its own is weak evidence: choose same or down from the rest of what they said, with lower confidence.
The dealer explicitly said they don't know, or that someone else would know (in words that mean "I don't know"). Not for a reply that is unclear, garbled or ambiguous: that is unclear.
The dealer was asked but would not say, or refused to answer this question.
The question was never asked, for example because the call ended first.

The question was asked and the dealer replied, but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question, so their answer can't be told. Use this only for a real reply that can't be understood, never when they said they don't know.

dispositions.name: loan_rejections
dispositions.question: Did the dealer say their customers' vehicle loan rejections, compared with last month, are happening more, about the same, or less? More than last month is high, the same is normal, less is low. If they describe a level instead of a change ("lots of rejections" = high, "normal" = normal), use that. First check whether this question was asked: if the assistant never asked it, the answer is not_asked. If it was asked (even once, even if a re-ask was cut off) it is never not_asked. objective_options.condition: Rejections are happening more than last month, or are high (for example കൂടുതലാണ്, കൂടി, bank strict).
Rejections are about the same as last month, or normal (for example അത്രയും തന്നെ, normal, നോർമൽ).
Rejections are happening less than last month, or are low (for example കുറവ്, കുറഞ്ഞു, എളുപ്പത്തിൽ approve).
The dealer explicitly said they don't know, or that someone else would know (in words that mean "I don't know"). Not for a reply that is unclear, garbled or ambiguous: that is unclear.

dispositions.name: outcome
dispositions.question: How did the call end? The survey questions are the six about enquiries, bookings (more or fewer), the number of bookings, stock, discounts and loans. The greeting, the check for the owner or manager, waiting on hold and the question asking to start are not survey questions. First count which of the six were asked or already answered. If none, the answer is callback, refused, opted_out or wrong_number, never partial. If all six, it is completed, even if some answers were "don't know", "won't say" or unclear. If some but not all, it is partial. opted_out needs an explicit request not to be called again (ഇനി call ചെയ്യരുത്). Just declining this time (വേണ്ട, interest ഇല്ല) is refused. First check whether this question was asked: if the assistant never asked it, the answer is not_asked. If it was asked (even once, even if a re-ask was cut off) it is never not_asked. If it was asked and the dealer's whole reply is only an acknowledgement (ശരി, അതെ, ഹം, ഓക്കേ), which does not pick an option, the answer is unclear. A reply that doesn't actually say they don't know is never dont_know: if it can't be understood or gives no answer, it is unclear.

objective_options.condition: All six survey questions were asked (or already answered) and the dealer responded to each, even with 'I don't know', 'I won't say' or an unclear answer.
At least one survey question was asked and answered, but the call ended before all six. Never choose partial when none of the six was asked.
Declined to take part, or didn't want the call recorded (for example വേണ്ട, interest ഇല്ല), without asking for a callback or to stop calls.
Asked to be called back at another time, or said the owner or manager isn't available, before the survey started (for example പിന്നെ call ചെയ്യൂ, ഇപ്പോൾ busy, വൈകുന്നേരം ചെയ്യൂ).
Asked not to be called again (for example ഇനി call ചെയ്യരുത്).
Not a vehicle dealership, or the wrong business or person entirely (for example wrong number, ഇത് showroom അല്ല).

dispositions.name: callback_time
dispositions.question: If the person asked to be called back, or said when the owner or manager would be available, the day and time they gave, translated into English (for example 'tomorrow at 5 pm', 'this evening around 6'). Leave empty otherwise.
